lesson.title: Review technical readiness: case exercise
lesson.summary: Review a technical deployment package for actual evidence gaps.

blocks: Case package: Northbridge supplies a current-version brochure, a test report for an older version, an automatic logging feature with no proven controlled-log custody, and a reviewer who cannot challenge scores.
The exercise supplies gaps, not proof of all possible faults. Review what each document actually demonstrates for the assessed version and intended use.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 11–15; Annex IV

blocks: A technical index needs the relevant records and explanations. Match purpose, design, datasets, oversight, test evidence and change history to the version. Listing a file does not establish its applicability.
If the old test still supports a claim, explain and evidence why. Otherwise request relevant testing rather than silently carrying the old result forward.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 11–15; Annex IV

blocks: Logging capability and custody are separate findings. Verify relevant automatic event recording and a qualified retention arrangement for logs under the actor’s control.
Oversight needs interpretation, anomaly handling, challenge and safe intervention. The supplied inability to challenge scores leaves a material readiness gap.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 11–15; Annex IV

blocks: Check purpose-appropriate accuracy and its declared metrics, fault resilience and appropriate AI-specific cybersecurity evidence. A good ordinary-input result does not answer every failure or attack case.

Supported decision: hold this evidence package pending resolved technical gaps and accountable actions. Conformity procedures, other law and actual deployment controls remain separate gates; this module does not grant market authorisation.
